matches.quote: The 1/3 exponent is not justified physically, and it is not stated whether it was fixed or free... show the sensitivity of p_c to the functional form
the experimental T_C collapse may need an additional cause, such as weakened intralayer exchange... include pressure-dependent intralayer exchange
No stacking enthalpies are given, so the claim that A-A "becomes stable" under pressure is unsupported... state the DOS structure.
The intralayer J1–J3 are taken from the ambient-pressure neutron study (Ref. [73]) and held fixed... include pressure-dependent intralayer exchange
The Fig. 4 caption is garbled ("a) ambient pressure, and a) a lower b) and c) lower than the transition temperature")
The measured stacking fraction does not follow the magnetic evolution... plot T_C(p), M_s(p) and the measured P-3m1 fraction on a common pressure axis
The measuring field is inconsistent: the Fig. 1 caption says 0.1 T, while the Fig. 1 legend... say 0.01 T (100 Oe).
The priority claim needs qualification... Refs. [18], [20], [24] and [39] already report pressure-dependent T_C or magnetization of CrBr3.
measure magnetization (high-field M(H) and low-field M(T)) of deliberately cut or deformed crystals with a large P-3m1 fraction next to as-grown R-3 crystals.
plot T_C(p), M_s(p) and the measured P-3m1 fraction on a common pressure axis
The text does not say how the "volume fraction of R-3" was obtained from single-crystal data (1/3-reflection intensities, refined Cr2 occupancy, or twin/phase scale factors)
The proposed mechanism and the spin model do not account for the collapse of the ordering temperature... The DFT does not address the pressure dependence the mechanism requires
Losing the 1/3 reflections means losing ABC order; it does not identify A-A registry... refine or simulate the competing models (A-A P-31m, random stacking, monoclinic faults)
It is not stated whether M(T) is ZFC or FC or how T_C was extracted (onset, inflection, dM/dT minimum)
The three probes give different critical pressures... Magnetization gives p_c ≈ 6.5 GPa (low temperature), XRD 6.4–8.4 GPa (300 K) and Raman ≈ 10–11 GPa (300 K)
the simulation assigns AA or AB coupling to randomly chosen atoms (p. 16), whereas a stacking fault flips the coupling across a whole layer interface
crystals that are already about 45% P-3m1 at ambient pressure... show the ideal CrBr3 values... report the phase fraction of the actual magnetization samples
not a 2/3-occupied 1a site in a 3.64 Å cell... state which stacking the DFT J_L = −0.35 meV refers to.

notes: The referees reviewed a condensed version where the magnetization curves were in Fig. S1 (moved to main-text Figs. 1-2 in arXiv v1, fixing C2, though the 0.1 T vs 0.01 T caption mismatch of C4 remained in Fig. 1). The Raman temperature (C6) is stated as room temperature on p. 4 of v1. An XRD phase-fraction plot (C10) is already present in v1 as Fig. 5b, so fixed_in_v1 is true for C10, while P5 and P17 still partly raise it by asking how the Fig. 5b fractions were extracted from the XRD reflections/refinement and how to quantify the AA stacking fault probability.
